ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of every natural person UBO, general partner, limited partner, and authorized signatory against HM Treasury sanctions lists, UN Security Council sanctions, OFAC SDN list, EU consolidated list, and Gibraltar's domestic sanctions regime. Enhanced due diligence is required for politically exposed persons (PEPs), including family members and close associates, using risk-based CDD under the Criminal Justice (Money Laundering) Act 2015. Negative screening results must be documented and stored for at least seven years. Failure to maintain adequate screening procedures constitutes a criminal offence and may also trigger statutory disqualification of the registered agent.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: English is the official language. Names must be submitted in Latin script. If the proposed name is in a non-Latin script, a transliteration into Latin characters is mandatory and must be accompanied by an accurate English translation. The name must not be offensive, misleading, or suggest an unauthorized legal form. An exempted limited partnership name must include the suffix 'Limited Partnership' or the abbreviation 'L.P.' as approved by the Registrar.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may file, within 21 days of the notice of refusal, a written administrative review request with the Gibraltar Companies Registry. The request must include a statutory declaration setting out the grounds for review, any supporting evidence of legitimate interest, and written consent from any affected statutory body where a sensitive token is involved. The Registrar is required to issue a written determination within 30 days. If the administrative review is unsuccessful, the applicant may file an appeal for judicial review in the Supreme Court of Gibraltar within 28 days of the determination. A name reservation may be extended for one further non-overlapping period of 30 days, upon payment of the applicable extension fee and provided no competing application has been lodged.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permitted. The ELP must maintain a physical registered office in Gibraltar to which official correspondence may be delivered and where the statutory records (register of partners, register of beneficial owners, and copies of limited partnership agreements) must be physically accessible. A registered office service provider is acceptable provided the premises are genuine commercial premises, not a PO Box, and are staffed during normal business hours. A virtual office or mail-forwarding-only address will not satisfy the requirement.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low for a low-risk franchise licensing and syrups supply chain ELP, estimated at approximately 5% per year for unannounced physical or compliance-file inspections. The likelihood increases to 20% or higher where the ELP is physically trading in Gibraltar, maintains local banking relationships, or is identified as high-risk in GFSC periodic reviews.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Limited Partnerships Act 2017 (Gibraltar), ss. 3-10 (registration and statement of particulars), s. 21 (exempted limited partnership status), s. 44 (annual statement obligations); Limited Partnerships Regulations 2018; Companies (Fees) Regulations 2018
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Companies, Gibraltar Companies House, under the administrative umbrella of the Gibraltar Financial Services Commission
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form LP1 (Application for Registration of a Limited Partnership) accompanied by the Statement of Partnership Particulars and the Consent to Act of the General Partner
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital or escrow deposit is required for an Exempted Limited Partnership; capital contributions are fixed solely by the Partnership Agreement. The ELP must at all times maintain a registered office in Gibraltar at the premises of a licensed fiduciary service provider and keep a beneficial ownership register at that office.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED by the Board of the Corporate General Partner of the Exempted Limited Partnership (ELP): (1) the Partnership Agreement attached as Schedule A is approved, and the General Partner is authorized to apply to the Registrar of Companies for registration under the Limited Partnerships Act 2017; (2) the initial capital contributions of the Limited Partners, detailed in Schedule B, are accepted and shall be credited to the capital ledger; (3) the registered office is established at the offices of the licensed fiduciary provider in Gibraltar, with authority to receive statutory notices; (4) [Name] is appointed initial manager with authority to open banking accounts and execute banking mandates; (5) the manager is authorized to file the statement of partnership particulars and all ancillary registrations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar Companies House, Registry of Business Names (online EFiling portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a public register name search and file a name reservation application. The proposed name must end with 'Limited Partnership' or 'L.P.' and must not contain restricted words (e.g., 'Bank', 'Insurance') unless an exemption is obtained. The licensed fiduciary submits the reservation electronically on behalf of the partners.
required_dossiers: Completed name reservation form (LP-NR1)
Certificate of name search results
Consent letter from the licensed fiduciary service provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected on grounds of similarity or restriction, amended name options are re-submitted within the same application cycle; the registration timeline pauses until name clearance is granted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Notarization of the Partnership Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public registered with the Supreme Court of Gibraltar and licensed legal counsel of the Gibraltar Law Society
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute the Partnership Deed detailing the general partner, limited partners, capital contributions, profit-sharing ratios, franchise royalty activities, and dispute resolution mechanism. All signature pages are notarized; the corporate general partner's board minutes approving the agreement are annexed. The notarized deed is then delivered to the fiduciary for the registration filing.
required_dossiers: Executed Partnership Agreement (notarized)
Board minutes of the corporate general partner approving the agreement
Certificate of incorporation and good standing of the corporate general partner
Passport copies of all individual partners and constitutional documents of entity partners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar or the fiduciary queries incomplete schedules, the agreement is re-executed and re-notarized within 5 business days without requiring a fresh name reservation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Registration Application and Statutory Fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, Gibraltar Companies House
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File Form LP1 together with the signed Statement of Partnership Particulars, the Consent to Act of the General Partner, the registered office declaration, and the beneficial ownership schedule. The filing fee is paid online via the Companies House EFiling portal, and a time-stamped acknowledgement is retained.
required_dossiers: Form LP1 (Application for Registration)
Signed Statement of Partnership Particulars
Declaration of registered office at the fiduciary's licensed premises
Consent to Act of the General Partner
Beneficial ownership schedule in the prescribed statutory format
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a query notice, the applicant must respond within 21 days by amending the Statement of Partnership Particulars and refiling electronically; no additional fee is charged for the first resubmission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, Gibraltar Companies House
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon satisfactory review, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Registration confirming the entity's status as an Exempted Limited Partnership. Counsel verifies the legal name, entity number, registration date, and exempt status against the public register before settlement of the banking mandate.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Registration of the Exempted Limited Partnership
Registered Statement of Partnership Particulars
Paid fee receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Any administrative discrepancy in the certificate text (e.g., name spelling or dated particulars) is corrected by filing a rectification request with the Registrar, with a 10 business day responsiveness guarantee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration and Beneficial Ownership Filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar Income Tax Office, HM Government of Gibraltar; GFSC-permitted corporate services provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notice of commercial activity to the Income Tax Office to obtain the tax reference number and confirm the ELP's tax treatment. File the beneficial ownership return through the licensed fiduciary. If the ELP will employ staff in the syrup production unit, register as a social insurance contributor and obtain a PAYE reference.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Registration
Notice of commencement of operations (tax form)
Partnership details declaration including pass-through allocation statement
Beneficial ownership register filing confirmation
Banking/KYC pack containing the structure chart and source of funds declarations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the beneficial ownership submission is rejected due to incomplete ultimate beneficial owner documentation, the fiduciary re-files the corrected schedule within 5 business days; the tax registration remains unaffected and proceeds in parallel.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Directorate of Environmental Health, HM Government of Gibraltar, in coordination with the Development and Planning Commission for premises approval
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Food Business Operator Registration and Beverage Manufacturing Permit under the Food Safety Act 2006, supplemented by a Licensing Notice for the production, storage, and distribution of bubble tea syrups and flavor bases

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Agency, Department of Environment, Heritage and Climate Change (DEHCC), HM Government of Gibraltar
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 2 - Screening and Registration; a full Environmental Impact Assessment Report is not required for syrup blending and warehousing under 100 tonnes annual throughput, provided a Site Environmental Management Plan is approved.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater effluent to sewer shall comply with the Gibraltar sewer discharge consent: pH 6.5-9.0, BOD not exceeding 300 mg/L, and TSS not exceeding 350 mg/L; VOC emissions from flavoring and sugar processing shall remain below 50 mg/m³; food-contaminated packaging and syrup residues shall be segregated and removed by a licensed waste contractor with a manifest trail.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate issued by HM Gibraltar Fire and Rescue Service following annual inspection of the production and storage premises; structural load and electrical installation clearance from Building Control at the Development and Planning Commission; occupational safety sign-off under the Health and Safety at Work (Gibraltar) regime, including a mandatory risk assessment and certification of all syrup-handling equipment.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: HM Government of Gibraltar – Income Tax Office (Commissioner of Income Tax) under the Ministry of Finance for direct taxation; Her Majesty's Customs, Gibraltar (Customs and Excise Department) for customs, import duty and excise obligations. Official portal: https://www.gibraltar.gov.gi (taxes section); Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (GFSC) electronic registry is the entry point for ELP formation and statutory filings.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Gibraltar Exempt Limited Partnership ('ELP') is first incorporated/registered with the GFSC under the Limited Partnerships Act 2015. For direct tax, the general partner must file the partnership registration particulars with the Income Tax Office and apply for a Gibraltar Tax Reference Number (TRN); each partner's identity, beneficial ownership and residence details must be disclosed. No VAT registration is obtainable because Gibraltar does not impose VAT/GST. The ELP must separately register as a Customs Declarant/Economic Operator with Gibraltar Customs if it imports or exports commercial goods. Standard supporting documents: partnership agreement, certificate of formation, registered-office certificate from a licensed local service provider, and partner residency/beneficial-ownership certificates.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible – the ELP is fiscally transparent under Gibraltar income tax law; the partnership itself is not an entity-level taxpayer. Each partner is chargeable on their respective share of Gibraltar-source profits (Income Tax Act 2010, as amended). Non-resident partners are taxable in Gibraltar only if a trade is carried on in Gibraltar and profits arise there; offshore franchise royalties and syrup-export co-ordination income may fall outside Gibraltar taxable income where the ELP lacks a Gibraltar trade nexus and complies with territorial-source rules.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists under Gibraltar law. The ELP is transparent by default; a partnership-agreement election that confers separate legal personality on the ELP does not convert it into a taxable entity for Gibraltar direct tax. Hybrid-mismatch counteraction rules aligned with OECD BEPS Action 2 and ATAD principles apply: a foreign-jurisdiction election to treat the ELP as opaque will be disregarded where it creates deduction/no-inclusion outcomes in the franchise royalty and syrup supply structure. A consolidated partnership return may be filed for administrative convenience, but assessed liability remains at partner level.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: No VAT / GST / Sales and Use Tax in Gibraltar (Gibraltar is outside the EU VAT area); the applicable indirect-tax regime is import duty and excise duty under the Customs Ordinance, supplemented by stamp duty on relevant documents.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: N/A – there is no VAT/GST registration threshold because no such tax exists. A person making commercial imports into Gibraltar must be registered as a customs declarant with Gibraltar Customs regardless of turnover; each import is subject to an electronic customs entry and payment of any applicable duty.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time e-invoicing, fiscal digital stamping or government clearance mandate exists for domestic supplies or services. Import/export entries are filed electronically through the Gibraltar Customs electronic entry-processing system; post-Brexit UK–Gibraltar Single Customs Territory applies to qualifying goods movements between Gibraltar and the UK. B2B invoices and royalty invoices must be retained in original audit-ready form but do not require pre-clearance or digital stamping.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is legally inapplicable because Gibraltar does not impose VAT/GST. For customs purposes, goods physically exported from Gibraltar to destinations outside the UK–Gibraltar customs territory are not chargeable to Gibraltar import duty on departure; duty-paid goods previously imported and subsequently re-exported may qualify for duty drawback. Offshore B2B services supplied by the ELP (franchise licensing, brand royalties, syrup-supply chain management) are outside the scope of Gibraltar indirect tax and may be excluded from Gibraltar direct tax as non-Gibraltar-source income, provided no trade is carried on within Gibraltar and the ELP meets applicable economic-substance and territoriality requirements.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Gibraltar Customs export declaration (electronic entry/SAD equivalent with export release number)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical removal from Gibraltar and, where relevant, export outside the UK–Gibraltar Single Customs Territory
Inward Remittance Certificate / bank SWIFT MT103 or equivalent evidencing receipt of franchise royalty and export-sale proceeds within 180 days
Franchise/master licence agreement, royalty invoice schedule and transfer-pricing documentation for the syrup-supply chain
Duty-paid import entry and drawback claim reference where re-exporting goods previously imported into Gibraltar
Beneficial ownership and partner tax-residence certificates substantiating the pass-through claim and hybrid-mismatch audit trail
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: False export, duty-drawback or offshore-service claims are subject to intensive audit scrutiny. Customs penalties under the Customs Ordinance include forfeiture of goods and monetary penalties of up to 200% of duty evaded, plus criminal prosecution for fraudulent declarations. Income-tax misdeclaration — such as booking Gibraltar-source franchise income as offshore royalties to avoid tax — attracts retrospective clawback (up to 6 years; extended to 20 years for fraud or neglect), surcharges up to 100% of the tax understated, interest, GAAR counteraction, and possible cancellation or disqualification of the ELP's registration. Non-resident partner documentation and economic-substance evidence are reviewed under UK–Gibraltar and OECD exchange-of-information arrangements.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Commissioner of Currency, H.M. Government of Gibraltar (currency issuance and maintenance of the Gibraltar pound at a fixed 1:1 parity with GBP under the Currency Note Act 1934); banking, e-money and FX conduct supervision vested in the Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (GFSC) under the Financial Services Act 2019 and Banking Act 2019.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility for current and capital account items; no exchange controls, no prior approval thresholds, and no withholding taxes on profit remittance or capital repatriation from a tax-transparent Gibraltar ELP. GIP and GBP circulate interchangeably at par; free conversion between GIP, GBP, EUR and USD is permitted, with only standard bank-level reporting. The ELP may denominate franchise agreements, trade contracts and bank accounts in any reserve currency.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender, forced conversion ratio, or retention timeline applies to export proceeds or service revenues in Gibraltar. Franchise royalty receipts and syrup-trade proceeds may be held indefinitely in their original currency; the only obligation is routine balance-of-payments statistical disclosure by regulated credit institutions for settlements at or above EUR 10,000 equivalent.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (GBP/EUR/USD) with segregated Capital Escrow Account for partner capital contributions
Operational Current Account (GIP/GBP) and Treasury Settlement Account
Cash Management Account with in-house FX desk; Trade LC issuance (MT700/MT760)
Operational Account; commercial banking suited to substance-backed ELPs
Digital multi-currency Operational Account (GBP/USD/USDC); corporate eligibility restricted
Private Banking Operational Account; high minimum asset thresholds

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: Medium-High. UK-authorised EMIs such as Wise Business, Revolut Business and Currencycloud routinely accept Gibraltar-registered entities under the UK-Gibraltar financial services continuity framework; non-UK EMIs without GFSC authorisation are not viable. EMIs may not accept deposits or extend credit, and all safeguarded funds must be held with a GFSC-licensed credit institution. Treasury cap: GBP 150,000 per EMI, swept daily to Barclays or Gibraltar International Bank to preserve purpose-code audit trails.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote-only opening is not guaranteed. GFSC AML/CFT guidance permits electronic identity verification for a Low_Risk_Standard entity, but bank policy prevails. Barclays (Gibraltar) and Gibraltar International Bank require an in-person KYC/EDD interview for at least one authorised signatory or general partner representative before first credit; Jyske and First Bank may accept video verification with a Gibraltar-licensed TCSP co-signing the CDD file. Budget for one on-island session with two working days lead time to satisfy the signatory mandate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-transparent ELP holding commercial substance only through a registered agent, with no employment or physical footprint in Gibraltar.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Substance file: Gibraltar lease and utilities; operating expenditure records; general partner and franchise management board minutes; statutory filings; payroll records for at least two Gibraltar-based employees; annual economic substance worksheet; transfer pricing documentation for all royalty flows.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO chain routed through the Cayman Islands (KY_ELP) and the United Kingdom, triggering layered-ownership scrutiny under FATF Recommendation 24.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete chain-of-title pack: Cayman registration certificate and good-standing letter; ELP partnership agreement and register of limited partners; UBO declarations with passport copies; licensed-CSP corroboration; group structure chart identifying all natural persons.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Royalty income comprising more than 75% of inflows, profiling the entity as an intellectual-property wrapper or base-erosion vehicle.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed boba tea franchise agreements; territory schedules and store lists; royalty computation schedules tied to audited franchisee revenue; trademark registrations; operational support logs; tax opinion confirming the ELP's historic pass-through status.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payments to Southeast Asian syrup and equipment suppliers with rapid outbound settlement across GBP, USD and CNH channels.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Master supply agreements containing Incoterms; supplier business licences; commercial invoices and transport documents (B/L or AWB); customs declarations; certificate of analysis; audited financial statements evidencing non-mixed use of wire profiles.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Multi-currency inflows (GBP/EUR/USD) generated without a documented treasury rationale, flagged as potential layering or round-tripping activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Formal treasury policy; hedging mandate designating future-dated forwards and NDFs; quarterly ALCO minutes; cash-flow projections; general partner distribution resolutions and remittance vouchers.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Routing: SWIFT MT103 from the Cayman ELP's bank, or from the UK service provider's client account, into the Barclays Gibraltar or Gibraltar International Bank operational account. Field 70 Remittance Information must carry ISO 20022 purpose code 'CTRD' for capital transfer or 'EQUI' for equity injection. Compliance protocol: general partner written resolution and capital contribution schedule; source-of-funds package comprising bank statements and audited accounts of the Cayman ELP; remit in GBP wherever possible to exploit the GIP/GBP parity peg and avoid conversion fees; if USD is remitted, convert immediately at the clearing bank's published rate and report to the balance-of-payments statistical return. The EDD file must evidence that funds derive from legitimate franchise operations, not personal wealth pooling.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Rails: (1) supplier payments for tea syrups and franchise equipment via SWIFT MT103/202 with purpose code 'TRAD' and strict invoice-matching instructions; (2) commercial letters of credit (sight, MT700) issued by Barclays or Jyske for recurring purchases from established Southeast Asian suppliers, with standby LC MT760 where a performance guarantee is demanded; (3) franchisee royalty collection and local POS aggregation through a payFac/API rail such as Adyen or Stripe, with same-day auto-settlement in GBP to the upstream treasury account; (4) each outbound instruction must carry a unique invoice reference and be pre-matched to the bank mandate to avoid unclassified disbursement triggers; (5) EMI balances may not execute trade settlement above EUR 50,000 per instruction.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable FX forwards (GBP/USD, GBP/EUR, USD/CNH) up to 12 months with a GFSC-licensed or OECD-licensed bank, executed under ISDA 2002 with collateral annex.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on CNY and franchise-territory currencies (THB, PHP, TRY) for non-convertible exposure; the ELP must post eligible collateral and record each NDF as a designated cash-flow hedge to preserve pass-through tax status.
Cross-currency swaps (GBP/USD, GBP/EUR, USD/CNH) for working-capital matching, with maturity aligned to franchise royalty cycles and documented ALCO approval.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return for Exempted Limited Partnership (Form LP-AR)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on the exact anniversary of the ELP's registration; filing permitted within 42 days after the anniversary. If the anniversary falls on a non-business day, the due date extends to the next business day.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing incurs a penalty of GBP 50 per month or part thereof, up to a maximum of GBP 600; continued default for more than 6 months may lead to a compliance notice, followed by administrative strike-off and dissolution of the ELP.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Gibraltar Registrar of Companies - Beneficial Ownership Secure Search (BOSS) System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On the same annual anniversary as the annual return, within 42 days of each registration anniversary; any change to UBO details must be reported within 14 days of the change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or maintain the UBO register is an offence punishable by a fine up to GBP 5,000; deliberate default may result in general partner disqualification and potential removal from the register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Gibraltar Income Tax Office (Commissioner of Income Tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 12 months after the end of the ELP's financial reporting period; for a calendar-year filer, no later than 31 December of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing attracts penalties from GBP 50 to GBP 500 per day for continued non-compliance; the Registrar may strike off the ELP after repeated failure.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent statutory audit is mandatory where (a) the ELP's annual turnover exceeds GBP 1,200,000; (b) its balance-sheet total exceeds GBP 500,000; or (c) it fails to qualify for the small partnership exemption under the Gibraltar Companies (Accounts) Regulations.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as issued by the IASB and adopted by Gibraltar law; alternatively, the ELP may apply UK GAAP (FRS 102) if it qualifies as a small entity under the Gibraltar Companies Act.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annually, by the ELP's anniversary of registration, every limited partner and the general partner must confirm to the registered agent that the beneficial ownership register is accurate. Any transfer of partnership interests or changes to shareholding percentages must be recorded in the UBO register and transmitted to the Registrar within 14 days. The confirmation must be endorsed by the general partner and filed simultaneously with the annual return.

stage_6.form_identifier_and_portal: Gibraltar Revenue Authority Corporate Income Tax Return (Form CTR-1) / Partnership Information Return (ESR-PIR) filed through GRA e-Tax online portal (https://www.gra.gi).
stage_6.reporting_frequency: Annual, once per accounting period (usually the calendar year for the general partner; partnership tax computation may be required even if ELP itself is transparent).
stage_6.statutory_deadline_rule: No later than 12 months after the end of the accounting period; for a 31 December year end, filing must occur before 31 December of the immediately following year. If the Commissioner issues a notice to file, a shorter 21-day period can apply.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Entity name, GRA tax reference number, Companies House Gibraltar registration number, registered office, EEA/EU? no; accounting period start/end; general partner identity; non-resident partner declarations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include the ELP’s GRA reference, name and address of the general partner, and confirm tax transparency; attach list of non-resident partners and their jurisdictions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross franchise royalties, syrup sale revenue, logistics fees, interest; deductible operating costs (COGS, marketing, software, amortisation); exclude non-taxable participation exempt dividends.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners must ensure no Gibraltar source trading income is omitted; treaty/economic substance basis should be stated in notes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Loss brought forward, capital allowances, foreign tax credits, participation exemption, arm’s-length transfer pricing adjustments, ESR-related deemed profits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim foreign tax credit/TRC at this section only if a DTA or unilateral relief is available; otherwise a reallocation may be challenged in GRA.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Chargeable profits multiplied by the 10% company/partner rate; withholding tax on non-resident partners if any (GIP statutory rate nil); balance of tax payable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No Gibraltar withholding tax on distributions to non-resident partners; if tax has been withheld by the payer overseas, claim a foreign tax credit here.
